points: Q2 returned to profitability with net income of $10.6 million on $184.1 million of revenue and a 91.0% operating ratio, but reports suggest equipment-sale gains helped; Q3 will show whether core operations can earn without that tailwind.

The CFI U.S. integration and unified technology platform were meant to lift consolidated performance; Q3 is the first print where those cost and revenue synergies should be visible in the operating ratio.
Consensus expects FY1 EPS of $0.19 and FY2 EPS of $0.50, a 168% year-two jump; Q3 needs to show the earnings recovery is on pace, not a one-quarter event.
ODFL, MRTN and WERN report just before HTLD in early November, so their freight-demand, pricing and margin commentary will set the read-through for HTLD’s Q4 setup.

The name carries a forward P/E of about 67x, roughly 1.8x the theme median, while the PEG is near parity; the long case therefore needs Q3 margin expansion and EPS momentum to make that growth valuation credible.
If Q3 delivers core profitability and integration savings, the setup into 2027 improves and the FY2 consensus of $0.50 looks reachable; if not, the premium multiple is vulnerable.
watch: Operating ratio improves from Q2’s 91.0% — supports the long.
Q3 operating revenue continues to grow year over year — supports the long.
Q3 EPS is positive and management commentary keeps FY1/FY2 consensus on track — supports the long.
Operating income is driven by freight operations rather than another large equipment-sale gain — supports the long.
